reviews.title: Very good
reviews.text: The current features are great, and the app could be even more effective with an option to prevent users from easily deleting it. Once you reach your limit for a certain app, it can be tempting to simply delete the restriction app altogether. It would be helpful to have a setting that allows users to lock the app from being deleted for a preset period (e.g., a few days or a week), with the option to schedule or change this lock at set intervals. This would make the app much more effective at helping users stick to their screen-time goals.

reviews.title: Exceptional app for anyone looking to reduce screentime
reviews.text:
I’ve seen and tried many apps that were advertised as effective methods of reducing your screen-time or limiting the apps you can open. They either let you pause the lock without restrictions, or they require a membership, which costs money — something a poor student like me would not appreciate. On the other hand, this app does not force you to incur monthly fees, or let you unlock your apps easily. Its strict mode, in particular, allows you to lock the apps you’re trying to avoid for no cost. There’s no way of unlocking apps while activating strict mode, which is a crucial feature for people who are seriously struggling with excessive screen usage and minimizing distractions. I’ve used this app throughout middle school, and now, in my freshmen year, my screen time has decreased significantly. In seventh grade, I spent nine hours on social media, which distracted me from schoolwork and hobbies. Now, I don’t even need the app, as I only spend around an hour or two daily on social media thanks to this feature. 

TL;DR: I highly recommend this if you want an app that effectively prevents you from accessing distractions at no cost.

reviews.title: Helpful, but too many glitches
reviews.text:
I’ve had premium for over a year and tried out most of the features. The app is attractive and clean. Simply blocking apps works well, including schedules. Strict mode works. 

I like the allowlist mode, but wish it allowed more than 50 (I know that’s Apple’s doing), because of all the apps I need to access to run various things in my house and my gym  - that’s 12 spots used up.

However, blocking by location does not work well. It doesn’t consistently turn off and on according to the set rules. 

Also, sometimes a block will gray out Messages and Reminders, like they were uninstalled but not removed, even though they weren’t included in the blocklist. 

Other times, a blocklist will be paused, but randomly block an app I’m actively using. 

So, this is a great app if you’ll only use the basic features, but not if you want to use the more advanced ones. Also, expect random glitches. Now that my year is up, I’m exploring other options.
